full_judgment: 16. Besides the above, in view of the testimony of plaintiff PW I as well as of PW 3, some Bashu Sikder, Akhtar Kazi and Abu Sayed are the important witnesses with regard to the alleged contract. But they being neighbours of both the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 and also being important witnesses have not been examined in this case, rather, the plaintiff examined some Mokbul Sheikh as PW 2 and Sona Mia as PW 3 who being closely related to the plaintiff belonging to different villages cannot be considered to be impartial and disinterested witnesses. Withholding of the aforesaid disinterested neighboring witnesses in the case by the plaintiff gives rise to a presumption that had they been examined in the case they would not have supported the plaintiffs case and, as such, the defendant No, 1 is entitled to get the benefit of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. Tender and refusal to accept the consideration money by the defendant No.1 has also not been proved and with this the plaintiff has totally failed to prove his cause of action in filing the suit.
